newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - June 24.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Co, which is responsible for its contents.
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BUDGET FEARS FAIL TO HALT PROPERTY RISE

The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors said the growth in momentum of the property market has been unaffected by the increase in interest rates or concern over the forthcoming budget. In the three months to the end of May, prices of homes in England and Wales rose 10 percent and the number of houses sold experienced a significant increase as well. The volume of houses sold remains below 1994 levels, leading observers to believe that the rise in revenues is due to an increase in prices due to overall housing shortages.
-- NIKE HAS A BALL ON THE TUBE

To boost awareness in London of its sponsorship of Wimbledon, Nike has 'recreated' centre court at the Southfields underground station, complete with marked and lined astroturf. At either end of the station platform are blown up pictures of Pete Sampras and Carlos Moya, with an 18-inch tennis ball suspended on a cable and travelling back and forth at a speed of about 20 mph. The advertising scheme reflects the recent relaxing of public transport policy in London.
THE TIMES
-- CWC AND TELEWEST IN 5.5 BLN STG LINK-UP TALK

British cable groups Cable and Wireless Communications and TeleWest Communications Plc are in talks to form a joint television and phone brand which could lead to a 5.5 billion stg merger between the two groups. The alliance would also increase their standing in the market share war against BSkyB and British Telecom, creating one of Europe's largest multi-media groups. TeleWest chairman Fred Vierra confirmed that the two groups were in talks and that the possibility of a 'full merger' could not be ruled out.
-- MISMATCH AT HARVEY NICHOLS

In its first full financial year as a public company, UK fashion retailer Harvey Nichols Group has reported pre-tax profits up one-third to 12.1 million stg on turnover of 114.2 million stg. The results are lower than had been predicted by the group's broker HSBC James Capel, who had penciled in pre-tax figures of 12.8 million stg.
-- DIGITAL TV RULING TODAY

The Independent Television Commission is to reveal on Tuesday the winner of the right to launch digital terrestrial television in Britain. The two groups battling for the bid are British Digital Broadcasting, which consists of Carlton and Granada and Digital Television Network, whose members are US cable company NTL and United News & Media. It is expected the loser of the bid will seek a judicial review of the decision.
THE GUARDIAN
-- REPORT INTO NATWEST MARKETS RULES OUT WIDESPREAD COLLUSION

A Coopers & Lybrand investigation into an options mispricing scandal which cost NatWest Markets about 90 million stg is expected to rule out widespread collusion between executives and Kyricos Papouis, the trader at the centre of the scandal. The results of the three-month long investigation should be released this week, and it is not expected that there will be any further dismissals or suspension, though a number of employees are likely to be disciplined.
-- STANDARD BOSS QUITS IN ROW

John Thomson has resigned from his 300,000 stg per year position at UK fund manager Standard Life after less than one year in the position. It is believed Thomson quit following a disagreement over corporate strategy and the company's failure to establish a fund management operation which could compete with groups such as Mercury asset management.
-- FRANCHISE INDUSTRY ON A HIGH AS IT SETS NEW RECORD

A survey on franchising in Britain based on results provided by 139 franchising systems and carried out by Lloyds TSB Bank reveals that most franchising companies are run by managers whose last position was as a small business entrepreneur. Of the 139 companies polled, 70 percent believed that franchising is set for steady growth, while 34 percent listed their greatest threat to survival as shortages of funds during the first two years of operation.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- LONRHO STAYS SILENT ON OUTCOME OF JCI MERGER

Sources from Lonrho Plc, the UK-based mining to hotels group have indicated that the outcome of merger talks between it and South African mining house JCI Ltd should be known within the next two months. Lonrho management, however, have stated that 'it is too early' to comment and 'there is no commitment' on the part of either party. Other groups said to be in the bidding for Lonrho include the Avmin and Gencor mining groups also from South Africa.
-- COMPASS PAYS 227 MLN STG FOR FRENCH CATERING GROUP

Compass, the largest catering group in Britain, has acquired a 93 percent stake in French food group Sodexho for 227.1 million stg, a move which is expected to close the gap between Sodexho and Generale de Restauration, the largest catering group in France. Compass is now set to sell its 1.2 percent stake in GDR, only six months after purchasing it due to disagreements concerning the group's 'strategy'.
-- GRANADA OFFER EXPECTED TODAY

Following a series of high-level meetings on Monday, the Granada Group is expected to forward a formal deal for the Yorshire-Tyne Tees Television group. Granada is confident it has the support of all shareholders - excluding Mercury Asset Management - for the 11.75 pounds stg per share acquisition and will circulate a 90-page offer document to all those holding shares.
